One million cubic meters through the ledger. Cities have been built with less material and worse attitude.

For one entire month, no belt was safe and no goblin out mined them. The rocks saw this one undock and quietly updated their wills.

The Sacred Choreography of Rock Acquisition
Module 2 · How We Run A Fleet

A fleet is what happens when a bunch of goblins agree to be in the same place and point their lasers at the same field of rocks at the same time, which sounds simple and is somehow the thing people mess up most. So here is the choreography. Learn it once and never ask in fleet again.
Step one. Get in the fleet.

The boosts, which are the reason you make real money instead of peasant money, only reach people who are actually IN the fleet. If you are mining next to the fleet but not in it, you are just a stranger nearby doing manual labor for free, like a raccoon going through the neighbor's trash. Be in the fleet.

We move as one. Together is faster, together is safer, and together means when something goes wrong we all warp out looking like professionals instead of one guy exploding alone while everyone watches.
Step three. Stay within 40km of the Orca.

The Orca is the big ship in the middle projecting an invisible bubble of pure yield around itself, and inside that bubble you mine roughly 83% faster. Eighty three percent. The moment you drift outside 40km, that bubble does nothing and your yield quietly collapses to the sad numbers of a man mining alone. Stay in the bubble. Get rich.

Position yourself so you can reach a fat field of rocks WHILE you are pointed at some faraway celestial. You stay pointed at the door the whole time. A goblin who mines aligned dies of old age. A goblin who mines sideways dies on a Tuesday.
Step five. When your hold is full, you do TWO things at once, every time, as one habit: you jetcan the ore, AND you log it in the ledger.

These are not separate tasks. Jetcan and log. Jetcan and log. Burn it in. Before the op even starts, open the Fleet Drop Ledger at bonkeve.com/fleet, punch in the fleet password and your pilot name, and leave it open. Then when your hold fills: jettison the ore into a can, and in the same breath select that ore with Ctrl+A, copy with Ctrl+C, paste it into the ledger, and hit Drop. The ledger now knows exactly what you dropped and you are on record to get paid for every unit.
Step six. The robots and the Orca handle the rest.

You do not compress your own ore. A little robot called the MTU reels your cans in automatically, like a Roomba for space rocks, and the Orca crushes the whole pile down when its hold is full and the grid is clear. You just keep mining, keep jetcanning, keep logging.
Step seven. The ore goes home, and Fear writes the checks.
And because you logged every drop, your check is exactly right, and nobody can argue about it.

Seven Rules That Cost Us A Lot To Learn

This is the most important module in the entire Academy. Every one of these seven rules was paid for. Not with theory. With ships. Real ones. Expensive ones. We learned them the hard way so you do not have to. In return you have to read seven bullet points. Deal.

None of these rules are obvious. That is the trap. Every one is the exact opposite of what your gut will scream at you in the moment. Your gut is going to get you killed. Follow the rules instead of the gut.

The instant you shoot, point, web, or send a drone at a hostile in highsec, you sign a permission slip that turns off your protection. That is a limited engagement. Our safety is not our guns. It is CONCORD, the space police, who delete anyone who attacks us, but only if we did not throw the first punch.
Your weapon is the warp drive. Your shield is CONCORD.
You do not have guns. Act like it.
Rule 2. Never help a corpmate who is already in a fight.

This one feels heroic and heroism is a trap. Rush in to rep him or send drones and you flag YOURSELF as a legal target too. You did not save him, you doubled the killmail. We have watched one loss become four this exact way.
Disengage, warp out, regroup, we reship the guy.
Rule 3. The Orca's Core stays down.

When the Orca turns on its Industrial Core it becomes a building. It cannot move, cannot warp, it is a very expensive statue. The boosts work fine without it, so the Core only comes up for one quick compress cycle when the hold is full and the grid is clear, then straight back down.
Rule 4. Watch local, but be a human about it.

You do not panic and dock up every time one neutral shows up. But a combat ship on the field, someone burning at you, a name you know is trouble? You are already aligned, so you just warp. Calmly. Use your eyes and use your head.
Rule 5. Your barge drones are for killing rats, not people.

Here is the trap: five barges see one 'lone' hostile and think 'we outnumber him.' The second your drones touch him, all five of you are flagged, and that lone hostile always has friends one jump away who were counting on exactly this. It is bait. It is always bait. The miners never fight.

Yes, again. Position so you can reach the rocks while holding an align off grid, so when trouble lands you are already leaving instead of sitting there ten agonizing seconds spooling your warp drive. Mine pointed at the door. Every time.

We have paid before, and we got shot anyway, every time, because a person who ambushes you for money is not bound by a strong code of honor. A ransom is a donation to the man about to kill you. Keep your wallet shut. We reship our own.

Core down, aligned out, local watched, nobody engages, nobody plays hero.

The whole job, in one loop

Mine rocks. Tell the ledger what you mined. Get paid your exact share when the op ends. This walkthrough shows the full loop once, including the part inside EVE. Thirty seconds, then you never think about it again.
Before the op: someone found this rock
Fleet command picks the spot with Radar, our belt scanner. You just fly where the fleet flies. If you ever want to scout your own, the Radar tool on the toolbelt knows every belt in New Eden.
Your ore is priced the moment you drop it

The ledger values every rock at live Jita prices, the market where everything actually sells. Buyback pays you a fixed cut of that, set for the op. No haggling, no spreadsheets, the math is already done.
In EVE: select what you mined
Open your ore hold or the can you filled. Click one stack, then Ctrl+A grabs them all. Partial stacks are fine. This is just selecting, nothing moves yet.

With the stacks selected, Ctrl+C copies them as text. Do this BEFORE you jettison or compress, while the ore is still in front of you. Then right click and Jettison for the hauler like normal. Copy first, dump second. That order is the whole trick.
Tell the ledger who you are
Pick the pilot the ISK should land on. Flying alts? Add each one once with + alt and tap between them. Every drop pays the name it was dropped under.
Click the box, Ctrl+V, hit Drop. The ledger reads the stacks, prices them, and adds them to your tab. Do this every time your hold fills. It becomes muscle memory by the second can.
The lazy way, once you have a rhythm
Grinding one ore all night? After the first drop it becomes a chip up here. Dial the number, tap drop, back to the belt. Chips reset each op so Monday's ice never haunts Thursday's Veldspar.
